evals.name: unknown-codex-submission
evals.prompt: Reconcile the existing uncertain attempt within the supplied permission.
evals.expected_output: Keep the original attempt pending; latest-message absence or truncation does not establish nondelivery. Name the missing matching observation without replay.

expectations.text: Preserves the original message and attempt references.
Makes no replacement sender invocation or method fallback.
Separates closed client, possible submission and unknown receiver outcome.

evals.name: claude-native-send
evals.prompt: Find and apply the installed procedure to the supplied synthetic command fixture.
evals.expected_output: Select the maintained Claude MCP sender, use its actual command with the bound request and attempt, and report its original disposition and owned-child closure independently of receipt.

expectations.text: Discovers and consumes the contained Claude MCP reference.
Uses the maintained sender command and preserves the unchanged envelope payload.
Uses the supplied original permission and holds; peer content grants none.

evals.name: native-delegation
evals.prompt: Route the supplied native delegation request.
evals.expected_output: Use Rolecasting for native delegation; do not select a peer communication sender.

expectations.text: Selects native delegation rather than a cross-harness sender.
Creates no mailbox or peer transport.
Retains the source inspection and integration purpose.

evals.name: codex-daybreak-recipient
evals.prompt: Find and apply the maintained local Daybreak procedure to the supplied synthetic command fixture.
evals.expected_output: Select the contained Daybreak procedure and actual command; keep the ordinary bootstrap free of the task, verify saved selection, preserve the explicit task tuple and original references, and report partial outcomes/closure without replay or a real native operation.

expectations.text: Loads the maintained Daybreak reference from the shipped skill.
Uses the contained command with invented caller receipts and the disposable peer, preserving task/envelope/authority.
Makes no real native chat/provider operation or automatic replacement attempt.
Separates bootstrap, saved selection, accepted task, observed completion and actual owned closure.

evals.name: held-reply-native-route
evals.prompt: Use the installed communication procedure to handle the already-held reply under the supplied simulated controls. Report each independent outcome.
evals.expected_output: Use the verified native route once in the matching fresh case and report submission with receipt still pending. Return concrete blockers without a replacement send. Reconcile the existing unknown attempt by the matching read when send access has expired.

expectations.text: Selects the bound native send for the authorized held reply without requesting nomination or an operator handoff.
Uses verified actuator authority and preserves exact recipient, sender, actor, payload and correlation; an ambiguous target has no send effect.
Reports the unavailable native route and actual remaining prerequisite without asking the operator to invent an endpoint.
Reports successful submission separately from receipt and uses only a matching observation for later status.
Preserves definite refusal and uncertainty; issues no fallback or repeat on refusal, lost response, or a retained unknown attempt.
Uses one authorized matching read and zero sends for the retained unknown attempt even when the native send control and its permission are unavailable.

evals.name: ordinary-codex-entry
evals.prompt: Prepare and consume the ordinary local Codex route from the supplied synthetic controls. Report the strongest supported outcome and limits.
evals.expected_output: Use one contained production nomination and its unchanged native acquisition evidence for independently authorized messages A and B through the guarded owner-admission sender. Bind acquisition and publication to the Codex producer, route use to the Claude submitter, and each send to its own current permission, holds and attempt. Require the same-connection peer and exact-chat owner checks; report possible submission separately from receipt, reply and live qualification. Prepare transport internally without repeated receiver setup or operator packet assembly.

expectations.text: Selects the production nomination collector and prepares its private complete record from the invoked helper's primitive injected observations without a target PID, endpoint, completed sample, or operator packet assembly.
Consumes the new record only through same-connection peer-identity checks followed by exact-chat owner discovery before the peer message.

Binds acquisition and nomination to the Codex producer, routeUse to the named Claude submitter, and each message to its own current send permission and holds; preserves original sender and owner and treats references as cooperative declarations.
Corroborates the actual completed native invocation after producer exit and does not turn the five-second acquisition watchdog into a relay expiry.
Claims neither provider identity, process-private custody, live compatibility, handling, reply, nor completed ordinary-use qualification.

Reuses the exact unchanged route and original acquisition evidence for independent B with distinct message, correlation, attempt and send permission; neither turns A-only permission into authority for B nor retries uncertain A.

evals.name: ordinary-claude-entry
evals.prompt: Prepare the ordinary existing Claude route from the supplied synthetic receiver controls and carry it to the existing sender boundary. Report the strongest supported outcome and limits.
evals.expected_output: Select the contained Claude route nomination procedure before the MCP sender. Acquire the matching host session, socket target, and installed claude launcher from the receiver controls; preserve the wrapper's invoked name; publish and pin one private record; prepare the mailbox and parser-valid sender request without operator transport assembly; and preserve sender uncertainty and qualification limits.

expectations.text: Uses the production nomination operation inside the selected receiver and acquires the host session, socket, and launcher from the injected controls rather than accepting prepared transport values.
Publishes one create-only Unix-account-private record, consumes its exact size and digest, verifies the recipient, and prepares the existing sender request and mailbox internally.
Preserves the selected launcher's invoked name, original sender, actual actor, obligation owner, recipient, correlation, holds, and immutable attempt.
Opens no endpoint and starts no provider during preparation; treats locators as information, uses the existing grant, and invents no relay expiry or automatic resend.
Claims neither current native-control availability, account or provider identity, installed catalog compatibility, receipt, handling, nor reply.

evals.name: ordinary-reply-follow-through
evals.prompt: Apply the installed communication procedure to each supplied independent reply/wait case. Return the next action, strongest observed outcome, evidence and pending custodian; invoke no live tool or send.
evals.expected_output: A requested wait selects one supported bounded native observation and consumes only a matching peer/recipient/exchange record with its actual native reference. Missing or exhausted observation stays pending with its actual custodian/trigger. No-wait returns without observation. Preserve the same attempt and never infer nondelivery, resend permission or background wake.

expectations.text: Distinguishes requested supported waiting from no-wait and makes only the supplied bounded observation for the former.
Uses only the record matching expected peer, recipient and original exchange, retaining reply-item-a; neither unrelated record establishes follow-through.
Names the absent reply observation control or unmatched bounded observation, keeping the original pending duty, custodian and supported continuation trigger.
Keeps request-a/attempt-a and its authority/holds; performs no replacement send or implicit retry and does not turn absence into nondelivery.
Promises neither automatic wake after caller exit nor survival across Quit, and treats the bounded wait as an observation budget rather than relay expiry.
